title: TODAY and NOW: the volatile clock

screens.prompt: In C2, work out how many days INV-1041 has been open, counting up to the day this exercise pins as today (15 March 2024).

hints.syntax: TODAY takes no arguments but keeps the empty brackets: =TODAY()-B2.
hints.func-today: Ask the clock for today rather than typing 15 March, because the column has to be right tomorrow as well.
hints.require-ref: Subtract the raised date in B2, so the next invoice needs a copy of the formula rather than new numbers.
hints.no-now: NOW carries the time of day, which leaves a fraction on the answer; TODAY is the whole number this column wants.
hints.value: 45366 minus 45352 is 14. A different figure usually means the reference slipped to a neighbouring row.
hints.error: #VALUE! means B2 holds the raised date as text, so TODAY has nothing numeric to subtract.

reject.why: today typed in as a number, so the column freezes at the day it was written
NOW is the moment rather than the day, and today's date is not in the formula at all
cancelling NOW back out still leaves the fraction of a day it carries
the date typed in, so changing B2 never reaches the answer
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0! instead of a count of days
one day too many — 15 instead of the 14 days INV-1041 has been open
the closing bracket is missing and TODAY takes no arguments anyway

screens.prompt: In B3, return the hour the stamp in B2 was taken at, with the exercise's clock pinned to 14:30.

hints.syntax: HOUR takes one date number and returns 0 to 23: =HOUR(B2).
hints.func-hour: The day sits left of the decimal point and the time right of it; HOUR reads the right-hand part.
hints.require-ref: Read the stamp in B2, since a retyped serial cannot carry the fraction exactly.
hints.value: 45366.604166667 is 15 March 2024 at 14:30, so the hour is 14 and not 604.
hints.error: Text in B2 gives #VALUE!, and a plain day number with no fraction gives 0 because there is no time to read.

reject.why: the minutes past the hour, not the hour
the stamp typed in, so a new reading never reaches the answer
TODAY is a whole day with no time on it, and the stamp in B2 is never read
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0! rather than an hour
the next hour on, 15 instead of 14
the hour turned into minutes, so 840
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs

docs.explain:
TODAY and NOW read the clock of the machine the workbook is open on, so their answer can change when nothing in the sheet has. TODAY returns the day as a whole serial, 45366 on 15 March 2024. NOW returns that day with the time since midnight in the fraction, so 14:30 is 45366.604166667. Both recalculate on every edit; Excel calls functions that do this volatile.

This sheet asks for days open, which is a subtraction. TODAY minus the raised date in B2 gives 14 for INV-1041. The second screen pulls the hour out of a stamp, because HOUR reads the fraction rather than the day. Building the first column on NOW leaves part of a day on the count.

Reach for TODAY when the answer is a date and NOW when the time of day matters. Volatile formulas recalculate on every edit, so a large sheet full of them is slower than one that reads a typed date from a single cell.

errors.text: HOUR was given a label rather than a date number, or the raised date in B2 was stored as text.
TODAY or NOW typed without the empty brackets, so Excel reads the name as an unknown word.
NOW keeps the time in the decimal, so a days-open column built on it shows 14.6 for a job that is 14 days old.

docs.atWork: An ageing report that counts days open each time the file is opened, and a log line stamped with the moment it was written.
docs.outcome: Tell today's date from this moment, and read the clock out of a date number.
docs.dataset: Invoices dated by day, and one log stamp timed to the minute

seo.title: TODAY and NOW in Excel: the clock functions
seo.description: TODAY gives the day as 45366, and NOW adds the fraction since midnight, so 14:30 reads 45366.604. Both recalculate on every edit, even with no change.
